title: Closed immersions descend to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ ($X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]) and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$. If $f$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $f_0$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then there is $i\ge0$ such that $f_i$ is a closed immersion (Stacks Limits, Lemma 01ZP).

source.place: Lemma Tag 01ZP (lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, line 1828) in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739); its proof: closed immersions are affine (Morphisms Lemma 01SE, lemma-closed-immersion-affine), Lemma 01ZN (descend-affine-finite-presentation) makes $f_0$ affine after increasing $0$, reduction to $X_0,Y_0$ affine over an affine $W\subseteq S_0$, and Algebra Lemma 07RH (lemma-colimit-surjective)

proof.text: *Step 1 (a stage where $f$ is affine).* Write $f_{ii'}:S_i\to S_{i'}$ ($i\ge i'$) for the transition morphisms, $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, and $p_i:S\to S_i$ for the projections of the limit. A closed immersion is affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc](b) (Stacks Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01SE), so $f$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-affine] (Stacks Limits, Lemma Tag 01ZN) there is $k\in I$, $k\ge0$, such that $f_k:X_k\to Y_k$ is affine. Fix such a $k$. (Source: 'A closed immersion is affine ... Hence by Lemma 01ZN after increasing $0$ we may assume that $f_0$ is affine.')

*Step 2 (replacing $0$ by $k$).* Let $T$ be $S_i$ for some $i\ge k$, with $q_T=f_{ik}:T\to S_k$, or $S$, with $q_T=p_k$; in both cases $f_{k0}\circ q_T:T\to S_0$ is the structure morphism $f_{i0}$, resp. $p_0$. Let $X_T=X_0\times_{S_0}T$, $Y_T=Y_0\times_{S_0}T$ and $f_T=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_T$ (so $f_T=f_i$, resp. $f$). (a) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to the diagram whose right column is $T\xrightarrow{q_T}S_k\xrightarrow{f_{k0}}S_0$, whose left column is $X_T\to X_k\to X_0$ (the first map being $(\mathrm{pr}_1,q_T\circ\mathrm{pr}_2)$ into $X_k=X_0\times_{S_0}S_k$, the second $\mathrm{pr}_1$), and whose horizontal maps are the second projections $X_T\to T$, $X_k\to S_k$, $X_0\to S_0$: the lower square is cartesian by definition of $X_k$ and the outer rectangle by definition of $X_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], so the upper square is cartesian, i.e. $X_T$ with $(\mathrm{pr}_1,q_T\mathrm{pr}_2)$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2$ is a fibre product $X_k\times_{S_k}T$. In the same way $Y_T$ is a fibre product $Y_k\times_{S_k}T$. Under these identifications $f_T$ and $f_k\times\mathrm{id}_T$ are two morphisms into $Y_k\times_{S_k}T$ with the same components ($\mathrm{pr}_1$ gives $(f_0\mathrm{pr}_1,q_T\mathrm{pr}_2)=f_k\circ(\mathrm{pr}_1,q_T\mathrm{pr}_2)$, $\mathrm{pr}_2$ gives $\mathrm{pr}_2$), hence equal: $f_T=f_k\times\mathrm{id}_T$. (b) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] to the diagram with left column $X_k\xrightarrow{f_k}Y_k\to S_k$, right column $X_0\xrightarrow{f_0}Y_0\to S_0$ and horizontal maps the first projections: the lower square ($Y_k$ over $S_k$) and the outer rectangle ($X_k$ over $S_k$) are cartesian, so the upper square is: $f_k$ is the base change of $f_0$ along $Y_k\to Y_0$. Since $f_0$ is locally of finite type, so is $f_k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change].

*Step 3 (finitely many affine pieces at stage $k$).* Write $g_0:Y_0\to S_0$ for the structure morphism. For $y\in Y_0$ choose an affine open $W\subseteq S_0$ containing $g_0(y)$ and an affine open $V\subseteq g_0^{-1}(W)$ containing $y$ ([lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]: an affine open is a spectrum, whose principal opens form a basis of affine opens). Since $Y_0$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], finitely many such pairs $(W_b,V_b)$, $b=1,\dots,m$, satisfy $Y_0=\bigcup_bV_b$, $g_0(V_b)\subseteq W_b$. Fix $b$ and drop it from the notation. Put $W_k=f_{k0}^{-1}(W)\subseteq S_k$, an affine open since $f_{k0}$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $V_k=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(V)\subseteq Y_k$. As $f_{k0}\mathrm{pr}_2=g_0\mathrm{pr}_1$ maps $V_k$ into $W$, $\mathrm{pr}_2(V_k)\subseteq W_k$, so $V_k=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(V)\cap\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(W_k)\cong V\times_WW_k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], which is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; the $V_{b,k}$ cover $Y_k$ (preimages of a covering) and $V_k$ maps into $W_k$. Since $f_k$ is affine (step 1), $U_k=f_k^{-1}(V_k)$ is an affine open of $X_k$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Put $A_k=\mathcal O_{S_k}(W_k)$, $B_k=\mathcal O_{Y_k}(V_k)$, $C_k=\mathcal O_{X_k}(U_k)$, with the ring maps $A_k\to B_k$ and $\varphi_k:B_k\to C_k$ induced by the structure morphism of $Y_k$ and by $f_k$; by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], under the identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] the restrictions $U_k\to V_k\to W_k$ are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of these maps. As $f_k$ is locally of finite type (step 2) and $f_k(U_k)\subseteq V_k$, $\varphi_k$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. (Only the quasi-compactness of $Y_0$ is used here.)

*Step 4 (the base over $W_k$ as a colimit of rings).* For $i\ge k$ put $W_i=f_{ik}^{-1}(W_k)$, an affine open of $S_i$ ($f_{ik}$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]), $A_i=\mathcal O_{S_i}(W_i)$, and for $i\ge i'\ge k$ let $A_{i'}\to A_i$ be induced by $f_{ii'}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] the restricted transition morphisms are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of these maps, and $(A_i)_{i\ge k}$ is a directed system over the directed set $I_{\ge k}$. Let $A=\varinjlim_{i\ge k}A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $W_S=p_k^{-1}(W_k)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] (the clause on open subschemes, with $k$ as the base index and $U_0=W_k$) $W_S$ is the limit of $(W_i)_{i\ge k}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] so is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the coprojections; uniqueness of limits gives $W_S\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, under which $p_k|_{W_S}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_k\to A)$. Write $A_T=A_i$, $W_T=W_i$ for $T=S_i$ and $A_T=A$, $W_T=W_S$ for $T=S$; then $W_T=q_T^{-1}(W_k)=\operatorname{Spec}A_T$ over $W_k=\operatorname{Spec}A_k$.

*Step 5 (the pieces of $f_T$ are spectra).* Let $T$ be as in step 2 and identify $X_T=X_k\times_{S_k}T$, $Y_T=Y_k\times_{S_k}T$, $f_T=f_k\times\mathrm{id}_T$ (step 2(a)). Put $V_T=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(V_k)\subseteq Y_T$ and $U_T=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(U_k)\subseteq X_T$. Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ f_T=f_k\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $U_k=f_k^{-1}(V_k)$, we have $U_T=f_T^{-1}(V_T)$. As in step 3, $\mathrm{pr}_2(U_T)\subseteq W_T$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2(V_T)\subseteq W_T$, so [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies $U_T=U_k\times_{W_k}W_T$ and $V_T=V_k\times_{W_k}W_T$, and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $U_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_T\otimes_{A_k}C_k)$ and $V_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_T\otimes_{A_k}B_k)$, the projections becoming $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $c\mapsto1\otimes c$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ (factors swapped by the symmetry of $\otimes$). The restriction $f_T|:U_T\to V_T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_{A_T}\otimes\varphi_k)$ are two morphisms into $V_T\cong V_k\times_{W_k}W_T$ with the same two components ($f_k|_{U_k}\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2$), hence equal; so, under these isomorphisms, $f_T|$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\varphi_T=\mathrm{id}_{A_T}\otimes\varphi_k:B_T=A_T\otimes_{A_k}B_k\to C_T=A_T\otimes_{A_k}C_k$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] the ring map $\mathcal O_{Y_T}(V_T)\to\mathcal O_{X_T}(U_T)=\mathcal O_{X_T}(f_T^{-1}(V_T))$ induced by $f_T$ is $\varphi_T$ composed on both sides with ring isomorphisms. For $T=S_i$ the opens $V^b_{S_i}$, $b=1,\dots,m$, cover $Y_i$, being the preimages of the covering $Y_k=\bigcup_bV_{b,k}$ (step 3).

*Step 6 (the hypothesis on the piece over $S$).* Take $T=S$ in step 5. $V_S$ is an affine open of $Y$ with $f^{-1}(V_S)=U_S$; since $f$ is a closed immersion, the ring map $\mathcal O_Y(V_S)\to\mathcal O_X(U_S)$ induced by $f$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1). By step 5 it equals $\beta\circ\varphi\circ\alpha$ with ring isomorphisms $\alpha,\beta$ and $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\varphi_k:A\otimes_{A_k}B_k\to A\otimes_{A_k}C_k$; hence $\varphi=\beta^{-1}\circ(\beta\varphi\alpha)\circ\alpha^{-1}$ is surjective.

*Step 7 (the algebra fact, and larger indices).* By steps 3 and 6, the directed system $(A_i)_{i\ge k}$ with colimit $A$ (step 4), the index $k$ and the $A_k$-algebra map $\varphi_k:B_k\to C_k$ of finite type satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-surjective-ring-map] (Stacks Algebra, Lemma Tag 07RH, with $k$ in place of $0$); so there is $i_b\ge k$ such that $\varphi_{i_b}:B_{i_b}\to C_{i_b}$ is surjective. This persists for every $i\ge i_b$: let $\tau:A_{i_b}\to A_i$ be the transition map; $\tau\otimes\mathrm{id}$ gives ring maps $B_{i_b}\to B_i$, $C_{i_b}\to C_i$ with $\varphi_i\circ(\tau\otimes\mathrm{id})=(\tau\otimes\mathrm{id})\circ\varphi_{i_b}$ (both send $a\otimes b\mapsto\tau(a)\otimes\varphi_k(b)$). For $c\in C_k$ write $1\otimes c=\varphi_{i_b}(\beta)$ with $\beta\in B_{i_b}$; applying $\tau\otimes\mathrm{id}$, $1\otimes c=\varphi_i(\bar\beta)$ in $C_i$, hence $a\otimes c=(a\otimes1)(1\otimes c)=\varphi_i\big((a\otimes1)\bar\beta\big)$ for $a\in A_i$ (as $a\otimes1=\varphi_i(a\otimes1)$). Since the $a\otimes c$ span $C_i$ additively and $\varphi_i$ is additive, $\varphi_i$ is surjective. (Source: 'The corresponding algebra statement is a consequence of Algebra, Lemma 07RH'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RH (lemma-colimit-surjective, line 47547), applied as in the proof of Limits Lemma Tag 01ZP

proof.text: *Step 8 (a common index; $f_i$ is a closed immersion).* $I$ is directed and there are finitely many $b$, so there is $i\in I$ with $i\ge i_b$ for $b=1,\dots,m$ (hence $i\ge k\ge0$; any $i\ge k$ if $m=0$). Take $T=S_i$ in step 5. For each $b$, $V^b_{S_i}$ is an affine open of $Y_i$, $f_i^{-1}(V^b_{S_i})=U^b_{S_i}$ is affine, and the ring map $\mathcal O_{Y_i}(V^b_{S_i})\to\mathcal O_{X_i}(U^b_{S_i})$ induced by $f_i$ is $\varphi^b_i$ composed on both sides with ring isomorphisms, hence surjective by step 7. The $V^b_{S_i}$ cover $Y_i$ (step 5), so $f_i$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2) (Stacks Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01QO).

Steps 2-5 (re-basing at k, finitely many affine pieces U_k -> V_k -> W_k with phi_k of finite type, the base over W_k as Spec of a colimit, the pieces of f_T as Spec of id_{A_T} (x) phi_k) are taken verbatim from the reviewed sibling lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite (01ZO), whose reduction is the same. Step 6: f closed immersion gives phi surjective over S (leaf lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion(1), 01QO).
